why: The copy shows a flat-topped 3-like sign marked sic, not the looped w, while Index A and C print w, so neither settles the sign.
The two lambda-like signs in yidotedikte are the same glyph in the printed formula C table and prose (d), and the same shape in the copy.
At high zoom the sign after ḫ is a large round S (e), unlike the small angular l of lowi beside it, and line 17 has the same word with e.
Index A prints ḫr[p]ḫli with ḫ outside the brackets, and the copy shows a black damaged sign at that place.
The copy shows two crossed strokes between soni and mni where the type prints only soni mnitowi, so an extra i is possible but not settled.
The damaged sign is a slash followed by a hook with a long bar, the te form of this copy, not slash plus a bare l.
Under the thin S of a the copy has a separate bold c-shaped sign open to the right, the ḫ form.
